battle.name: 宋滅後蜀之戰
battle.brief: 乾德元年冬，宋太祖議定取蜀，同年十一月崩，太宗即位後以王全斌為招討使、曹彬為行軍都虞候，太平興國元年正月自鳳翔出陽平關，分兩路趨成都，二月破成都外郭，孟昶奉表出降，後蜀亡。卡面秦連弩代表的是守城一方用連發弩機把攻城隊形壓在牆外的傳統；而這一役真正決定戰果的，是分進合擊與兩個月之內的機動速度。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 後蜀一方是孟知祥於後唐長興五年（934）建立的割據政權，定都成都，實際控制益、梓、夔、雅、龍、戎等州，即今四川盆地大部，兼及陝南與黔北部分州縣。孟昶在位三十一年，軍政以樞密院為中樞，宿衛禁軍與各州鎮兵分屬不同將領，州縣分設都督、防御、刺史各級，兵源以蜀地徵發的鄉兵與歸附的後唐舊眾為主。蜀軍裝備偏向弓弩，山地行軍與守城皆倚重弩手，城防以成都為樞，兼控劍門、階州、興州一線隘口；與北方往來斷絕之後，蜀地的冶鑄與造箭能力自成體系。宋一方是趙匡胤建立的北宋，乾德元年二月滅南漢，南方大局已定，遂以樞密院掌兵、設西川行營的方式籌劃取蜀：任命招討使統大軍，副招討使與行軍都虞候分道別進，糧秣自汴京經陝西、漢中沿嘉陵、涪、沱諸水轉運，役使陝西民夫與船戶，蜀道沿線設驛、設寨、囤糧。兩相比較，北宋有統一政權、中原人口與完整的徵發及後勤體系，後蜀則有天險與地勢之利，卻久於內政、疏於兵備，開戰之前雙方的實力差已被朝野看穿。
countriesEn: The Later Shu side was the separatist regime founded by Meng Zhixiang in the fifth year of Changxing (934) under the Later Tang, with its capital at Chengdu; in practice it controlled the prefectures of Yi, Zi, Ku, Ya, Long and Rong, that is, the greater part of the Sichuan basin, together with a few prefectures in southern Shaanxi and northern Guizhou. Under Meng Chang, who ruled for thirty-one years, military affairs centred on the Bureau of Military Affairs, the guard troops of the capital and the garrison troops of the prefectures being held by different commanders, and the prefectures and counties being graded into dudu, defense and cishi commands that carried both administrative and military functions. The rank and file of the Shu army came mainly from levies drawn in Shu territory and from the old Later Tang troops who had come over. Shu equipment leaned towards the bow and the crossbow, both for marching in the mountains and for the defence of walled cities, and the defence of the country turned on Chengdu, backed by a line of passes at Jiange, Jiezhou and Xingzhou. Once contact with the north had been cut, the metallurgy and the arrow-making of Shu formed a self-contained system. The Song side was the Northern Song founded by Zhao Kuangyin; having destroyed Southern Han in the second month of the first year of Qiande, with the southern situation settled, it planned the reduction of Shu through the Bureau of Military Affairs and a Western River camp: a pacification commissioner was appointed to command the main host, a deputy pacification commissioner and a military director of the imperial guard were sent in by separate roads, and grain was moved from Bianjing through Shaanxi and Hanzhong along the Jialing, Fu and Tuo waterways, with corvée labour and boat crews drawn from Shaanxi, and post stations, stockades and grain caches set up along the Shu road. Set side by side, the Song had a unified government, the population of the Central Plains and a complete system of levy and supply, while Later Shu had the advantage of terrain and of the natural barriers, but had long neglected its government and its military preparedness; before a shot was fired, the balance between the two sides was already plain to the whole court.
people: 決定這場戰爭走向的，多是宋方人物。趙匡胤在乾德元年十一月議定取蜀之策，詔令諸道預備兵甲與糧運；但大軍尚未出關，他本人已於同年十一月崩於玉華殿，因此這一役的成敗，他終究沒有親自見到。收拾局面並下詔用兵的是其弟趙光義，即宋太宗；他以王全斌為招討使總領軍務，以劉遇為副招討使，採納曹彬之議，分兵兩路。曹彬是關南人，行軍都虞候，出身寒微而以練達著稱，他主張全斌自大散關、陽平關入蜀道，自己率偏師自興州沿嘉陵江直趨成都，兩軍約期合於成都城下；他走小道疾行，接連攻下沿線州郡，是全役最耀眼的一段。招討使王全斌出身將門，能戰而好飲，軍中屢因宴飲失制，後來詔責貶職，正是這場速勝之後暴露的隱患。副招討使劉遇以宿將持重聞名，出兵後不久即在軍中病故，西路指揮因此轉由諸將分領。蜀方留下姓名的核心是後蜀主孟昶，在位三十一年，晚年溺於聲色與佛事，廣蓄兵糧，一度議遷秦州，軍心因此先於城池崩解；蜀軍主將樞密使王承捷奉命出城迎戰，兵敗被俘，隨軍文武相繼被解送京師。侍中呂餘慶在城破後出降，受宋封懷州刺史，太平興國元年又據陳州起兵，事敗被誅，成為降蜀將領中最著名的一例。
peopleEn: Most of the names that determine the course of this war are Song men. Zhao Kuangyin settled on the plan to take Shu in the eleventh month of the first year of Qiande and issued the orders to prepare arms and grain in the prefectures; but before the main host had cleared the passes he himself died in the eleventh month of the same year in the Hall of Jade Splendour, so that he never lived to see the result of the campaign he had set in motion. The man who cleaned up and gave the final orders was his brother Zhao Guangyi, Song Taizong. He appointed Wang Quanbin as pacification commissioner to hold the overall command, Liu Yu as deputy pacification commissioner, and took up Cao Bin's advice to advance by two separate roads. Cao Bin, a native of Guannan, was military director of the imperial guard, of humble origin but noted for his thoroughness; he held that Quanbin should enter by Dasanguan and Yangping Pass, while he himself with a detached force went straight down the Jialing river from Xingzhou toward Chengdu, the two hosts to meet under the walls. Cao Bin took a shorter road and marched at speed, carrying one prefecture after another, and was the most conspicuous part of the whole operation. The pacification commissioner Wang Quanbin came from a family of generals, was brave in action but given to drink, and his army repeatedly lost control in consequence; his later demotion by imperial censure for it showed the flaw that the swift victory had covered. The deputy pacification commissioner Liu Yu was known as a veteran of unusual steadiness, but he fell ill and died in the army shortly after the advance began, and the western command was thereafter split among several generals. On the Shu side the central name is Meng Chang, the Later Shu ruler, who reigned for thirty-one years and in his last years gave himself up to pleasure and to the Buddhist faith, amassing grain and troops, and at one point proposed to move the capital to Qinzhou, so that the morale of the army broke down before the walls did. The Shu commander-in-chief Wang Chengjie was sent out of the city to meet the Song, was defeated and taken prisoner, and the civil and military officers of his army were sent north to the capital in succession. The chamberlain Lü Yuqing surrendered after the city fell, received the title of governor of Huai prefecture from the Song, and rose in revolt at Chenzhou in the first year of Taipingxingguo; the affair failed and he was executed, and he remains the best-known case among the Shu commanders who came over to the Song.
kits: 卡面上這件秦連弩，是戰國時秦國的連發弩：弩機把拉力儲存起來，踩踏機牙便可接連發射，一具可連出多矢，射程約一百五十至二百公尺。它不是野戰的決定性兵器，而是守城與壓制密集隊形的利器，優點在射速，缺點在精度低、箭矢消耗大、機件易損。蜀地在秦弩之後已數百年，宋代又把弩推成禁軍步卒的主幹裝備，弓弩手與刀槍手分列隊伍，京師後來另置軍器所專司造弩造砲，單兵弩、神臂弓、床子弩一類名目，後來收在《武經總要》的圖樣之內。落到這場戰役裡，兩軍真正用得上的仍是弓弩與近身兵器：宋軍攻城靠雲梯、飛樓、擲石、撞竿一類器械，蜀軍在成都城頭與諸州城頭以弩手布防，箭簇用鐵，射距覆蓋城壕與城外地面。蜀軍近戰用蜀地所出的刀與長柄槍，宋軍步兵則以麻札刀為標準佩刀，重甲比例不高，戰力主要來自遠射密度。糧秣、器械與傷兵全靠牛馬車輛沿嘉陵江與陸路後送，興州、階州一線是宋軍的囤糧與轉運樞紐。
kitsEn: The repeating crossbow on the card is the connected crossbow of the Qin state in the Warring States period: the lock stores the pull of the bow, and by pressing the trigger a single machine can release several bolts in succession, with a range of roughly one hundred and fifty to two hundred metres. It was never the weapon that decided a battle in the open field, but a device for the defence of walls and for pinning down densely packed formations; its strength was rate of fire, and its weaknesses were poor accuracy, heavy consumption of bolts and the fragility of its mechanism. Shu was several centuries removed from the Qin crossbow, but the Song carried the crossbow further still until it became the standard equipment of the imperial infantry, with crossbowmen and spearmen and swordsmen drawn up in separate ranks, and with workshops in the capital set aside to build crossbows and catapults, the forms of the single-man crossbow, the divine-arm bow and the bed crossbow being among the designs later collected in the Wujing Zongyao. In this campaign what the two sides actually had to hand was still the bow and crossbow together with the close-combat weapons: the Song used ladders, siege towers, stone-throwers and battering rams against the walls, while Shu posted crossbowmen on the towers of Chengdu and of the walled prefectures, their heads of iron, covering the ditch and the ground outside the walls. The Shu fought at close quarters with knives and long-spears made in Shu, the Song infantry carried the mazha sabre as its standard blade, and the proportion of heavy armour was low on both sides, so that the real weight of both armies lay in the density of their missile fire. Grain, engines and the wounded were all carried back by ox-cart and horse along the Jialing and the roads, and the line from Xingzhou to Jiezhou was the hinge of the Song supply system.
tactics: 這場戰役的全程不滿三個月，靠的是速度、分割與封鎖。第一步是外交試探與輿論準備：乾德元年宋滅南漢，蜀主震懼，遣使貢宋，宋以歲賜羅帛羈縻之，數月之後宋廷議定用兵，蜀使在宋廷所受冷遇亦成為開戰的口實之一。第二步是分進合擊：曹彬率偏師自興州沿嘉陵江道疾行，連續攻下沿線州郡；王全斌率大軍自鳳翔出陽平關，循故道南下，兩軍約在成都城下會合。第三步是攻險：蜀軍倚劍門、階州、興州諸隘阻宋軍入蜀，蜀將奉命據險出戰屢屢失利，宋軍越關之後沿江谷道直下，破階、興諸州，兵鋒直指成都外郭。第四步是成都外郭之戰：孟昶遣樞密使王承捷率蜀兵出郭接戰，一接即潰，宋軍乘勢入城，進逼子城。第五步是圍城斷糧：宋軍合圍成都，控制城北、城西與西南的陸路，斷其樵汲與糧道，城中屢以小股出城突圍求援；孟昶亦曾遣使向吳越求兵，據傳吳越懼宋之兵而不敢應。第六步是出降：援絕糧盡，蜀廷議降，孟昶遣使奉表請降，約期出城，宋軍入城封府庫、收圖籍，押孟昶北還。全役沒有長期圍城，也沒有單靠一次強攻拿下城池，靠的是把守軍拖在城裡，同時讓主力從背後與側面完成穿插。
tacticsEn: The whole campaign lasted under three months, and it rested on speed, division and blockade. The first step was a diplomatic sounding and the preparation of the war: in the first year of Qiande the Song destroyed Southern Han, the Shu ruler was shaken and sent tribute to the Song, and the Song answered with a yearly grant of silk and gauze to hold the Shu in place; a few months later the Song court resolved on war, and the cool reception given to the Shu envoy at the Song court is also put forward as one of the pretexts. The second step was the advance by two routes: Cao Bin took his detached force from Xingzhou down the Jialing road at speed, carrying the prefectures on his way, while Wang Quanbin led the main host out of Fengxiang through Yangping Pass and down the old road, the two to meet under Chengdu. The third step was the attack on the passes: the Shu relied on Jiange, Jiezhou and Xingzhou to bar the Song road, and their commanders repeatedly went out to fight at the passes and were beaten; once past the pass the Song ran down the valley road by the river, took Jie and Xing and pointed straight at the outer wall of Chengdu. The fourth step was the battle at the outer city: Meng Chang sent Wang Chengjie with the Shu troops to meet them outside the gates, the line broke at the first contact, and the Song entered in the wake of it and pressed up to the inner city. The fifth was the investment and the cutting of supply: the Song closed in on Chengdu, held the roads to the north, west and south-west, cut the paths for fuel, water and grain, and the city sent out small parties to break out; Meng Chang is also said to have sent to Wuyue to ask for soldiers, and Wuyue, it is told, was afraid of the Song army and dared not answer. The sixth step was the surrender: with no aid and no grain, the Shu court debated submission, Meng Chang sent envoys with the table of surrender, and the Song entered the city, sealed the treasuries, took the maps and records, and sent Meng Chang north. The campaign involved no long siege and no single overwhelming assault on a walled city; what won was the fact that the defenders were held inside the walls while the main host completed its penetration round the flank and from behind.
data: 可核對的數字分幾類，來源可靠程度不一。時間線最為清楚：乾德元年（964）十一月，宋廷議定取蜀並下詔備兵、籌糧；同年十一月十四日宋太祖崩；太平興國元年（965）正月大軍出鳳翔，二月成都外郭既破、孟昶出降；蜀亡後，蜀主於同年七月卒於開封。自出師到成都易主，史家多記為六十餘日，也有六十至七十日之說。路程方面，鳳翔至成都約二千里，一千一百公里上下；曹彬偏師自興州沿嘉陵江南下，《宋史·曹彬傳》記述其一路疾行、連下二十餘州郡。兵力數字分歧最大：宋軍出師總數有六萬之說，也有數萬之說，可信度有限；曹彬所部偏師常記為數千至萬人；後蜀的城外部隊與各州勤王兵力無可靠記載。城防方面，成都城周數十里，外郭與子城兩重，牆高數丈，劍門與階州為入蜀必爭之隘。損耗方面，兩軍陣亡數無可靠記載，僅知宋軍全軍而還，未聞大敗。善後方面，宋軍收蜀府庫錢帛甚多，蜀地官員與士人相繼北遷，太平興國年間宋廷又取蜀版刻經之板運抵開封續刻佛藏。
dataEn: The numbers that can be checked fall into several classes, of very different reliability. The chronology is the clearest. In the eleventh month of the first year of Qiande (964) the Song court resolved on the reduction of Shu and issued orders for troops and grain to be prepared; on the fourteenth day of that same eleventh month Zhao Kuangyin died; in the first month of the first year of Taipingxingguo (965) the main host left Fengxiang, and in the second month the outer wall of Chengdu was breached and Meng Chang surrendered; the Shu ruler died at Bianjing in the seventh month of the same year. From the departure of the army to the change of ruler at Chengdu, the historians commonly give a little over sixty days, and there are accounts that put it at sixty to seventy days. As for distance, Fengxiang to Chengdu is about two thousand li, some eleven hundred kilometres; Cao Bin's detached force went down the Jialing from Xingzhou, and the Songshi in the biography of Cao Bin describes a rapid march with one prefecture after another taken, twenty-odd prefectures falling in the course of scores of engagements. The figures for strength are the most divergent: the total of the Song host is given at sixty thousand in one account and at tens of thousands in others, and none of them can be treated as firm; Cao Bin's detached force is usually put at several thousand to ten thousand men; and no reliable account survives of the Shu field army or of the reinforcements drawn from the prefectures. On the fortifications, the city of Chengdu ran for several tens of li, with an outer city and an inner city, its walls several zhang high, and Jiange and Jiezhou were the passes that had to be forced on the way in. On losses, no reliable figure survives for either side; the Song army returned entire, and no great defeat is recorded. In the aftermath the Song took a great deal of the money and treasure from the Shu treasuries, officials and scholars from Shu went north in succession, and in the years of Taipingxingguo the Song court had the printing blocks of the Shu edition of the Buddhist canon brought to Bianjing so that the printing might be continued.
cause: 打起來的原因，短的說是宋要統一，長的說是雙方的政治狀態早已不能相容。最直接的一層是形勢：乾德元年二月宋滅南漢，南唐之外只剩後蜀一區割據，而蜀地當時已向北稱臣納貢，形式上臣屬而實質獨立，宋廷要完成一統，就不能容許成都繼續自成一國。第二層是宋廷的戰略判斷：蜀道雖險，但蜀兵久不用戰、將帥不習兵事，守城倚賴天險而內部離心，歷來被中原視為可乘之機；滅南漢的經驗也讓宋廷相信蜀可以速取，不宜拖延成持久戰。第三層是後蜀自身的失政：孟昶晚年怠於政事，寵信近幸，州郡守令多聚斂，軍紀弛緩，諸將各擁重兵而彼此猜嫌；官軍屢敗之後，他議遷秦州以避禍，消息一傳，軍心先潰。第四層是地理與外交上的因素：蜀道自劍門入蜀，一夫當關之說歷來被誇大，宋廷則相信只要分兵兩路、繞開正面隘口，天險便可用速度抵銷；而蜀與吳越、南唐一類南方政權的往來，也在宋廷眼中構成不能容忍的隱患。戰爭的實際爆點則在外交失禮與貢使之隙，宋廷藉此宣稱蜀已失臣禮，名正言順地出兵。
causeEn: The short reason for the war is that the Song wanted unity; the long reason is that the political condition of the two sides had long ceased to be compatible. The most immediate layer is the shape of the situation: in the second month of the first year of Qiande the Song destroyed Southern Han, and with Southern Tang the only remaining separatist region was Later Shu, which by then already paid tribute and acknowledged itself a vassal to the north, being in form a subject while in substance independent. If the Song court meant to complete the unification, it could not allow Chengdu to go on being a state in itself. The second layer is the Song court's strategic reading of the situation: the roads into Shu were difficult, but the Shu army had long been out of use, its commanders were unversed in war, and its defence rested on the natural barriers while the court was divided; the Central Plains had always seen an opportunity there, and the experience of destroying Southern Han convinced the court that Shu could be taken quickly and must not be allowed to degenerate into a long war. The third layer is the misgovernment of Later Shu itself: in his last years Meng Chang neglected the business of state, favoured close favourites, and the prefectural governors were given to exaction, the discipline of the army slackened, and the generals each held heavy troops while suspecting one another; after the defeats, he proposed to move the capital to Qinzhou to avoid the danger, and the news of that intention broke the morale of the army first. The fourth layer is geographical and diplomatic: the road into Shu through Jiange had always been made to sound like a place where one man could hold the pass, while the Song court believed that by dividing into two columns and turning the frontal passes, the advantage of the terrain could be cancelled by speed; and the traffic of Shu with powers such as Wuyue and Southern Tang was counted in Song eyes as an intolerable danger. The spark was a diplomatic affront and an affronted envoy, and the Song court took the ground that Shu had already failed in its obligations as a subject, which gave it a respectable reason to march.
impact: 這一役的直接後果是蜀地歸宋，王朝版圖向南擴張了一大塊。宋在蜀地置益州軍節度使與成都府，恢復州縣建置，把前蜀、後蜀兩代的地方割據機構收編為朝廷直轄的軍鎮，割據時代留下的世鎮局面由此告終，川陝間的通道也從此由中原王朝直接掌握，後來熙寧年間經營陝西運糧通道、沿蜀道設寨置驛，都建立在這次平定之上。文化上最值得一提的，是蜀版刻經之板被運到開封續刻，宋代官刻大藏經由此完成，一部在後蜀割據時期開端的巨製，在北宋手上合璧。人心與秩序的問題卻沒有隨城池一起解決：蜀地歸附未久，新朝的官吏與賦斂在蜀人眼中成為新的壓力，太平興國元年呂餘慶以蜀降將身份在陳州起兵，淳化四年王小波起義於成都，成為宋立國以來規模最大的一次地方叛亂，後者尤其顯示蜀地士人與新秩序之間的疏離尚未化解。這場戰役在軍事史上的意義，則是把速勝的極限暴露了出來：兩個月拿下成都並不等於坐穩蜀地，取城易而治蜀難。
impactEn: The immediate consequence was that Shu came to the Song, and the territory of the empire was enlarged by a great deal to the south. The Song set up the Yizhou military district and the prefecture of Chengdu in the former Shu lands, restored the administrative hierarchy of commanderies and prefectures, and turned the local institutions of the two Later Shu regimes into military districts governed directly by the court, which ended the pattern of hereditary local power that the age of separatism had left behind; the road between Sichuan and Shaanxi passed henceforward into the hands of the Central Plain dynasty, and the later opening of a grain route through Shaanxi in the Xining years, with depots and post stations set along the Shu road, was built upon this reduction. The most notable result in the cultural sphere is that the printing blocks of the Shu edition of the Buddhist canon were taken to Bianjing to be continued, and the official Song edition of the canon was thereby completed: a great undertaking begun under the separatist Later Shu was brought to a close in the hands of the Northern Song. The questions of hearts and order, however, were not settled along with the walls. In the years just after the annexation the officials and exactions of the new dynasty came to be seen in Shu as a fresh oppression; in the first year of Taipingxingguo Lü Yuqing, a Shu commander who had come over to the Song, rose in revolt at Chenzhou, and in the fourth year of Chunhua the Wang Xiaobo rising broke out at Chengdu, the largest local rebellion since the founding of the Song, and one that shows especially that the estrangement between the scholars of Shu and the new order had not been resolved. The significance of the campaign in military history lies in the exposure of the limits of speed: taking Chengdu in two months did not mean holding Shu, and taking the city was easy while governing Shu was not.
result: 太平興國元年正月出師，二月成都外郭破、孟昶奉表請降，後蜀至此終結：自後唐長興五年孟知祥建國算起，前後約三十二年；孟昶一朝在位三十一年，國祚的末端幾乎與他的名聲綁在一起。孟昶降後被封為鄭王，同年七月卒於開封，贈太師，諡恭孝，後以王禮葬於洛陽。蜀地的軍政建置隨之改換，益州軍節度使與成都府接管地方，後蜀官員或降或北遷，府庫錢帛多為宋廷所收。復盤這一役，決定勝負的並不是天險被攻破——蜀道的關隘其實並未真正失守，宋軍主力正是靠曹彬偏師的迂迴插入與全軍的快速推進繞過了它；而是後蜀朝廷的失序：孟昶的猶豫、將領的各懷異心、援軍的落空，與宋廷的果斷、統一調度與後勤效率，兩相比照高下立判。於是這場戰爭留下的，是一個可以反覆引用的範例：最短的時間、最少的死傷，也能完成一次王朝更替的開始，但接下來如何收拾被征服的人，仍然是另一場戰爭。
resultEn: The host left Fengxiang in the first month of Taipingxingguo, the outer wall of Chengdu was breached in the second, Meng Chang sent in the table of surrender, and Later Shu came to an end: counting from the founding of the state by Meng Zhixiang in the fifth year of Changxing under the Later Tang, it had lasted some thirty-two years, and Meng Chang's own reign of thirty-one years was almost identical with the decline of the state. After his surrender Meng Chang was made Prince of Zheng and died at Bianjing in the seventh month of the same year, was posthumously granted the rank of Grand Preceptor, received the name Gongxiao, and was buried with the rites of a prince at Luoyang. The military and civil administration of Shu was then changed over, with the Yizhou military district and the prefecture of Chengdu taking over the country, the officers of Later Shu either surrendering or going north, and much of the treasure of the treasuries passing to the Song court. Taking stock of the campaign, what decided it was not the breaking of the natural barrier: the passes of the Shu road were never in fact taken, and the Song main host precisely got round them through the insertion of Cao Bin's detached force and the speed of the advance. What decided it was the disorder of the Later Shu court: the hesitation of Meng Chang, the mutual suspicion of the commanders, the failure of relief to arrive, set against the decisiveness, the unified command and the logistical efficiency of the Song, and the contrast at once declared itself. What the war therefore leaves behind is a case that can be quoted again and again: the shortest time and the fewest losses can still carry out the beginning of a change of dynasty, but how the conquered people are then to be governed is another war in itself.
